role.altitude: The pediatrician keeps examining, deciding, prescribing and talking with children and parents; looking up weight-based doses, typing consultation notes and finding leaflets shrink a little.
skills_to_grow: Validating drafted notes quickly and spotting what a scribe left out
role.ambitious_version: A pediatrician who looks at the child and parents during the consult instead of the screen.

tasks.short: Have the child's weight measured, decide the treatment, calculate the weight-based dose, prescribe medication or vaccination in the record, administer or supervise the treatment and record what was given.

steps.what: Pediatric nurse weighs and measures the child and records it in the record
Pediatrician decides the treatment, therapy, medication or vaccination for the child
Pediatrician looks up the children's dose and calculates it from the child's weight
Pediatrician prescribes the medication in the record and handles interaction and contraindication alerts
Pediatrician administers the treatment or vaccination, or supervises the nurse doing it
Pediatrician records the medication or vaccine given, with batch number and time, in the record

tasks.design: The prescribing screen in the hospital record ({OPS_SYSTEM}) computes the children's dose from the weight the nurse measured today and the dosing rules loaded with the drug database, and the existing medication checks flag interactions, contraindications and doses out of range. The pediatrician checks the proposal and signs; nothing is prescribed without them. When a medicine or vaccine is given, scanning the package barcode records product, batch and time. Deciding and treating stay with the pediatrician; no model is used.
tasks.previous_blocker: Children's doses were looked up and calculated by hand, and batch numbers typed from the package.
tasks.enabler_now: Drug databases with dose rules and barcode scanning at the point of care.
tasks.still_hard: Off-label use in young children, where dose rules are thin.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing a treatment the family can actually manage at home.
tasks.altitude: A little less calculating and typing; prescribing stays with the pediatrician.

reach.learn: Whether calculated doses cut pharmacist queries on children's prescriptions.

evidence.claim: The Dutch drug database checks interactions, contraindications, doses and duplicates, with content set by the pharmacists' association.
A prescription must come from a named practitioner; software drafts, it does not prescribe.
The health inspectorate names medication errors from wrong registration as a risk of new software.

assumptions: Boundary: from the measured weight to the administration record; explaining treatment is a separate task.

Input contract for s3: the child's actual weight measured today by the nurse in s1, and pediatric dose rules in the drug database loaded in the hospital record ({OPS_SYSTEM}); for drugs without a rule (about half of prescriptions in young children) the pediatrician still looks up the dose; s3 is priced at that share.
Input contract for s6: package barcodes on about 80% of medicines and vaccines given; the rest are typed.
Deciding and administering keep their full time; nurse time is outside the pediatrician's savings.
unknowns: Share of children's prescriptions covered by dose rules in the hospital's system.

already_counted.description: Pediatrician checks calculated doses against the clinical picture before signing.

incremental.description: Pediatrician reports wrong or missing dose rules to the pharmacy.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: an outpatient clinic with few prescriptions; high: a ward with many weight-based prescriptions and vaccinations.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take the history from parents and child, examine patients, write the consultation note, order and interpret diagnostic tests, determine the diagnosis and record its code.

steps.what: Pediatrician takes the history from the parents and child
Pediatrician examines the child
Pediatrician writes the consultation note with history and findings in the record

loop.input: The audio of the consultation, recorded with the parents' consent, and the note template for pediatrics.
loop.output: A draft note with history and findings in the template's headings.
loop.check: The pediatrician validates and edits every note before it is written to the record; a monthly sample of notes is compared with the audio for omissions.
loop.stop: One draft per consultation; nothing is written to the record without validation.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates give headings; the history comes as conversation.

steps.what: Pediatrician orders laboratory tests and imaging in the record
Pediatrician interprets the diagnostic test results
Pediatrician determines the diagnosis and records the diagnosis code

loop.output: Suggested diagnosis codes from the hospital's code list.
loop.check: Only codes on the hospital's list are offered; the pediatrician picks or rejects; the diagnosis itself is theirs.
loop.why_not_simpler: Code search needs the right term; the note already holds it.

tasks.design: With the parents' consent a certified scribe records the consultation and drafts the note in the pediatric template; the pediatrician validates every note before it reaches the hospital record ({OPS_SYSTEM}). From the validated note the scribe suggests diagnosis codes from the hospital's list. History, examination, ordering, interpreting and the diagnosis stay with the pediatrician; no software interprets results.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes were typed during or after the consult, with eyes on the screen.
tasks.enabler_now: Scribe tools that write into Dutch hospital records after validation, carrying MDR class IIa.
tasks.still_hard: A child who cannot say what hurts.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing what the parents are worried about but not saying.
tasks.altitude: A little less typing; diagnosis stays with the pediatrician.

reach.learn: Whether suggested codes change coding corrections.

evidence.claim: A Dutch scribe records the consultation, the clinician validates, and the note goes into the hospital record.
In a Swedish health system, 1,295 clinicians using a scribe self-estimated note time falling from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes (29%); three of seven authors from the vendor.
Ambient recording captures staff performance and needs works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from history to coded diagnosis; explaining results is a separate task.

Input contract for s3: consultation audio recorded by the scribe with the parents' consent, given in about 80% of consultations; the rest are typed; the 29% note time cut from the Swedish case is applied to that share.
History, examination, ordering and interpreting keep their full or nearly full time.
unknowns: Share of parents who agree to recording.
research_questions: Do validated notes miss findings the pediatrician would have typed?

already_counted.description: Pediatrician validates and edits each drafted note.

incremental.description: Pediatrician asks parents for consent to record and notes it.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: parents often decline recording and short consults; high: long outpatient consults with most parents agreeing.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Advise patients, parents and community members concerning diet, activity, hygiene and disease prevention in the consult, give vetted leaflets, answer follow-up questions, give talks and note the advice.

steps.what: Pediatrician advises the child and parents on diet, activity, hygiene and disease prevention in the consult
Pediatrician finds and gives leaflets and links for the parents
Pediatrician answers parents' follow-up questions sent through the patient portal

loop.input: The parent's question and the hospital's vetted patient texts and public guideline-based texts.
loop.output: A draft reply that quotes the relevant paragraph and links to it.
loop.check: Every statement must cite a paragraph from the vetted texts, or it is dropped; anything about this child's treatment is written by the pediatrician, who signs every reply.
loop.stop: One draft per question; questions outside the texts get no draft.
loop.why_not_simpler: Parents ask in their own words; the right paragraph has to be found.

steps.what: Pediatrician advises community members such as schools and child health clinics in talks and meetings
Pediatrician notes the advice given in the record

tasks.design: The hospital's leaflet library is linked to diagnosis codes in the hospital record ({OPS_SYSTEM}), so the leaflets for this diagnosis are offered and sent to the parents' portal with one click. Portal questions get a draft reply quoting vetted texts, which the pediatrician edits and signs. The advice itself, talks for schools and clinics, and the note stay with the pediatrician; the advice note is part of the validated consultation note where a scribe is used.
tasks.previous_blocker: Leaflets were searched per family, and portal questions answered from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Guideline-based public patient texts, and leaflet libraries linked to diagnosis codes.
tasks.still_hard: Advice families cannot follow because of money, time or culture.
tasks.human_edge: Finding the one change a family will actually make.
tasks.altitude: Less searching and typing; advice stays with the pediatrician.

reach.learn: Whether linked leaflets cut repeat questions.

evidence.claim: A public Dutch patient information site is written with the GP and specialist associations and the patients' federation, based on guidelines.
A patient chatbot must disclose AI; here the pediatrician signs every reply, so no chatbot talks to parents.

assumptions: Boundary: health advice to families and the community; treatment decisions are separate.
Input contract for s2: leaflets linked to diagnosis codes by the outpatient clinic's nurse specialist; diagnoses without a link are searched as today; about 60% are covered.
Input contract for s3: parents' questions in the portal; vetted texts maintained by the hospital's patient information office.
Advice in the consult and in the community keeps its full time.
research_questions: Do parents read the leaflets sent to the portal?

incremental.description: Pediatrician flags outdated leaflets to the patient information office.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: advice mostly given in person; high: chronic conditions with many portal questions.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review results before the talk, explain procedures and discuss test results or prescribed treatments with patients and parents, answer their later questions and record the conversation.

steps.what: Pediatrician reviews the test results and plan before the talk
Pediatrician explains procedures and discusses test results and prescribed treatments with the child and parents
Pediatrician answers parents' questions afterwards by phone or portal
Pediatrician records the conversation and agreements in the record

loop.input: The audio of the conversation, recorded with the parents' consent.
loop.output: A draft note of what was explained, the parents' questions and the agreements.
loop.check: The pediatrician validates and edits the note before it is written to the record.
loop.why_not_simpler: The agreements come out of a conversation, not a form.

tasks.design: The conversation stays fully human. With the parents' consent the same scribe used in consults drafts the note of what was explained and agreed, and the pediatrician validates it before it goes into the hospital record ({OPS_SYSTEM}). Bad news conversations are not recorded unless the parents ask for it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Nothing blocked the talk; only the note took typing.
tasks.enabler_now: Validated scribe notes in Dutch hospital records.
tasks.still_hard: Explaining a serious diagnosis to frightened parents.
tasks.human_edge: Choosing words a child of this age can bear.

reach.task: Follow up families after bad news
reach.learn: Whether a clear conversation note helps follow-up calls.

evidence.claim: A Dutch scribe drafts the note and the clinician validates it before it enters the record.
Providers are responsible for careful use of generative AI: risk assessment, training, testing and monitoring.

assumptions: Boundary: explaining results and treatments; the decision itself is a separate task.
Input contract for s4: conversation audio recorded by the scribe with the parents' consent, in about 70% of these talks; the rest are typed.
Preparation, the talk and later questions keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of talks parents allow to be recorded.
research_questions: Do parents recall agreements better when the note is complete?

incremental.description: Pediatrician asks parents for consent to record.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: short talks and few recordings; high: long treatment talks with most parents agreeing to recording.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
